game-2d.desc: complete 2D arcade engine (canvas, touch joystick + keyboard + dash, sound, particles, combo, difficulty ramp, menus) with a playable demo
game-2d.guide: Keep the engine (loop, input, sound, overlay, HUD plumbing). Replace the content: the world, the art, the rules.
customize: Redraw every entity with theme-specific art built from canvas paths (not plain circles): player, collectibles, hazards, and a themed background with parallax layers or scenery.
Add at least two mechanics the template does not have (power-ups such as shield or magnet, a second enemy behavior, shooting, waves or a boss, a dash upgrade, levels).
Rework the menu, HUD and game-over screen to match the theme: title treatment, real instructions, themed colors and typography, floating +score text.
Add varied sound events (and a small procedural music loop if it fits) and visual feedback for every event.
Add progression: levels or waves with a clear difficulty curve, and persist useful state (best score, settings).

game-3d.desc: complete Three.js r128 arena game (follow camera, joystick + keyboard, gems, chasers, particles, menus)
game-3d.guide: Keep the engine (renderer, camera, input, states). Replace the world, the models and the rules.
customize: Build themed models from grouped primitives for the player, gems and enemies (not plain spheres), and give the world props, a sky or fog color that fits the theme, and landmarks.
Add at least two mechanics the template does not have (power-ups, a second enemy type, obstacles, a goal or level system, a dash or jump).
Rework the menu, HUD and game-over screen to match the theme, with real instructions and a title treatment.
Add particles and camera feedback for events (collect, hit, power-up) and a difficulty curve across levels or waves.
Keep performance in check: shared geometries and materials, no allocation in update(), capped pixel ratio.

web-landing.desc: responsive accessible one-page site (hero, features, steps, pricing, FAQ, contact form) with light and dark themes

vars.TITLE: Brand
vars.DESCRIPTION: One or two sentences that say what it is and who it is for.

web-landing.guide: Keep the design tokens, accessibility and responsive behavior. Replace the identity, the content and the layout.
customize: Create a distinct brand identity: a palette beyond one accent (surface, ink, secondary tone), a deliberate type pairing or weights, and a shape language that fits the subject.

Replace EVERY placeholder with real, specific copy; remove sections that do not apply and add the ones that do (gallery, timeline, comparison table, case studies, team, location), with real structure for the subject.
Design a custom hero visual with inline SVG or CSS illustration instead of the generic preview card.
Vary the layout from the template (split sections, bento grid, large type, alternating rows) while keeping spacing tokens.
Add tasteful interactions (hover and reveal states, a sticky call to action, a working form handler or filter) and a footer with real links.

web-app.desc: single-file app shell (state/render, add/edit/delete with undo, filters, search, dialog, shortcuts, localStorage)
web-app.guide: Keep the state -> render -> events structure. Replace the domain, the fields and the views.
customize: Model the real domain: change the item fields, labels, validation and sample data to fit the request.
Add at least two features beyond the template (a summary or stats view with inline SVG charts, sorting, tags or categories, import/export, due dates, drag to reorder).
Give it a distinct look: its own palette, spacing and typography, better empty states and microcopy, not the starter's skin.
Add keyboard shortcuts and accessible announcements for every new action, and persist the new fields with a bumped storage version.
Handle errors visibly (invalid input, failed save) with clear messages.
